text.p: Investors in Electroscope Inc filed a complaint with the U.S. District Court of Minnesota alleging the company made false statements about its revenue, plaintiffs' lawyers said on Friday.

The case, which "is seeking to be maintained as a class action," according to the lawyers, was brought by investors who bought shares during Electroscope's June 25, 1996 initial public offering and up to February 7, 1997.
No one was immediately available at Electroscope to comment on the case.

In a statament, the attorneys also said their complaint also cites John G. Kinnard & Co, the lead underwriter of Electroscope's initial public offering, and the members of Electroscope's board of directors.

They said the compplaint specifically charges the defendants omitted information about net revenue growth related to a one-time sale to its distributor, and reduced net revenue for the first fiscal quarter ended three business days after the initial public offering.
The plaintiffs attorneys did not specify a dollar amount in damages that they would seek.
Reached for comment later, Carl Hawkins, acting chief financial officer for Electroscope, said he had no knowledge of the case.
